title: Initial nondegenerate object in each simplex comma category
statement: Use simplicial sets, standard simplices, ordinary nerves and weak contractibility of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $X$ be a small simplicial set such that every nondegenerate simplex $\Delta^n\to X$ is injective in every degree. Nondegenerate means not obtained from a lower-dimensional simplex by a nonidentity surjective simplex operator. Let $C=\mathsf S(X)$ have all simplices as objects, with arrows $\rho:\Delta^n\to X\ \longrightarrow\ \tau:\Delta^m\to X$ the monotone maps $\alpha:[n]\to[m]$ satisfying $\tau\Delta(\alpha)=\rho$, composed as monotone maps. Let $B_X\subseteq C$ be the full subcategory on nondegenerate simplices. For a simplex $\sigma$ of $X$, let $(\sigma\downarrow B_X)$ have objects $(\tau,a:\sigma\to\tau)$ with $\tau\in B_X$, and arrows $(\tau,a)\to(\tau\prime,a\prime)$ the morphisms $h:\tau\to\tau\prime$ in $B_X$ with $h a=a\prime$. Write $\sigma=\bar\sigma\Delta(s_\sigma)$ for the unique nondegenerate decomposition of [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-set-nondegenerate-decomposition]. Then $(\bar\sigma,s_\sigma)$ is initial in $(\sigma\downarrow B_X)$: it has exactly one morphism to each object. The nerve $N(\sigma\downarrow B_X)$ is weakly contractible.

source.place: HTT Variant 4.2.3.15, step (5), printed p. 256; initial-object and contractibility argument expanded here. Online source read 2026-10-17; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Fix a simplex $\sigma:\Delta^n\to X$. By [lem-weil-pbc-simplicial-set-nondegenerate-decomposition] there are a nondegenerate $\bar\sigma:\Delta^r\to X$ and a surjective monotone $s_\sigma:[n]\twoheadrightarrow[r]$ with $\bar\sigma\Delta(s_\sigma)=\sigma$. Thus $c=(\bar\sigma,s_\sigma)$ is an object of $D=(\sigma\downarrow B_X)$ by its displayed definition. The category $D$ is small: its objects are pairs of a simplex of the small $X$ and a monotone map of finite ordinals, and its arrows are subsets of the finite sets of monotone maps between the corresponding ordinals. Its nerve and the weak-equivalence convention are those of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones].

source.place: HTT Variant 4.2.3.15(5) and Variant 4.2.3.16, first paragraph, printed p. 256 (PDF page 274); explicit agent expansion of the universal-arrow and nerve-contraction argument. Read online 2026-10-17; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Let $d=(\tau,a)$ be any object of $D$. The hypotheses of [lem-coef-nondegenerate-simplex-face-poset] hold: $X$ is small and every nondegenerate simplex is degreewise injective, which is precisely its monomorphism condition. Its factorization clause gives exactly one $t:\bar\sigma\to\tau$ in $B_X$ with $t\circ s_\sigma=a$. By the definition of morphisms of $D$, such $t$ are exactly the morphisms $c\to d$. Therefore each such hom-set has exactly one element, so $c$ is initial. This uses the factorization clause, not just the poset clause, and concerns all simplex operators $a$, including noninjective ones.

source.place: HTT Variant 4.2.3.15(5) and Variant 4.2.3.16, first paragraph, printed p. 256 (PDF page 274); explicit agent expansion of the universal-arrow and nerve-contraction argument. Read online 2026-10-17; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Let $P:D\to\mathbf 1$ be the unique functor to the one-object, one-arrow category and let $Q:\mathbf 1\to D$ select $c$. Then $PQ=\mathrm{id}_{\mathbf 1}$, while $QP$ is the constant functor at $c$. The unique arrows $\eta_d:c\to d$ of step 2 define a natural transformation $QP\Rightarrow\mathrm{id}_D$: for $h:d\to d\prime$, both $h\eta_d$ and $\eta_{d\prime}$ are arrows from $c$ to $d\prime$ and hence are equal. Apply [lem-coef-nerve-natural-homotopy-equivalence] to these small categories, with this one-link transformation for $QP$ and the identity transformation for $PQ$. It gives that $NP:N(D)\to N(\mathbf 1)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. By the ordinary nerve formula in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], $N(\mathbf 1)$ has exactly one simplex in each degree and all operators are the unique functions, so it is $\Delta^0$ and $NP$ is the unique map to it. By the definition of weak contractibility in that same node, $N(\sigma\downarrow B_X)$ is weakly contractible.

lean.statement: theorem initial_nondegenerate_simplex_comma (X : SSet.{u}) [X.Nonsingular] (s : X.S) : ∃ d : SimplexDecomposition X s, (∀ d' : SimplexDecomposition X s, d' = d) ∧ (∀ q : simplexCommaCategory X s, Nonempty (decompositionCommaObject d ⟶ q) ∧ ∀ (f g : decompositionCommaObject d ⟶ q), f = g) ∧ SSet.Enhanced.IsContractible (nerve (simplexCommaCategory X s))
